# Enola CLI — Full Context for LLMs

> Enola CLI builds private infrastructure on Linux: self-hosted services that bind only to 127.0.0.1 and are reachable exclusively through the Tor network — with system hardening applied by default and releases verifiable offline. Deploy targets include Tor hidden services (.onion), Git servers (Forgejo), CMS platforms (WordPress, Drupal, Ghost, Magnolia, Strapi, Wagtail), anonymous file sharing, WireGuard VPN, UFW firewall and AppArmor sandboxing on Debian/Linux — with post-quantum signed releases (ML-DSA-65, FIPS 204).

## What it is

- Product: `enola-cli`, a single Rust binary for end users. Current version: 0.10.0-alpha.
- Purpose: privacy-first self-hosting. Every service binds to 127.0.0.1 only and is exposed exclusively through Tor hidden services. Traffic model: `.onion:VIRTUAL_PORT → Nginx:INTERNAL_PORT → App:TARGET_PORT`.
- Platform: Debian/Linux (x86_64). Requires root (sudo), Docker, Nginx, Tor. `enola-cli setup` installs dependencies.
- License: source-visible proprietary. Free for personal, non-commercial use. No redistribution, no commercial use. Copyright (c) 2026 Salvador Palma Rodriguez.
- Security reporting: vulnerabilities must be reported privately to salvadorpalmarodriguez@gmail.com within 72 hours of discovery; public disclosure is prohibited until remediation (license §5).
- Architecture: hexagonal (ports & adapters). domain (pure logic) / ports (traits) / adapters (Docker, Nginx, Tor) / application (orchestration) / cli (routing) / infrastructure (utilities).

## Installation

```
curl -fsSL https://github.com/SalvadorPalmaRodriguez/enola-cli-lite/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sudo bash
```

The installer verifies SHA256 + minisign signature. Downloads can additionally be verified offline with the embedded post-quantum key: `enola-cli verify <file>`.

Offline / tarball mode: the `*-client.tar.gz` asset is self-contained (binary + `install.sh` + `uninstall.sh` + `enola-cli.sha256`). After verifying the tarball's `.minisig` and extracting it, run `sudo bash install.sh` inside the directory: it installs from the bundled binary without downloading anything.

Installer environment variables: `ENOLA_INSTALL_BASE_URL`, `ENOLA_INSTALL_VERSION`, `ENOLA_INSTALL_PREFIX`, `ENOLA_INSTALL_NO_VERIFY`, `ENOLA_INSTALL_PUBKEY`, `ENOLA_INSTALL_STRICT_PUBKEY`, `ENOLA_INSTALL_SKIP_DEPS` (skip the `enola-cli setup` + `setup --security` dependency bootstrap), `ENOLA_INSTALL_FORCE_DOWNLOAD` (force a remote download even when a local binary sits next to `install.sh`).

## Command reference (complete tree)

Global options: `--format text|json`, `--verbose`, `--binary-base-url <URL>`, `--web-url <URL>`, `--docs-url <URL>`, `--tor-socks <URL>`.

### tor — Tor hidden services
- `tor list` — list services with .onion addresses and ports
- `tor create -n <name> [-s web|static|files|raw] [-p <virtual-port>] [-t <target-port>] [--ssl]` — create a hidden service
- `tor start|stop <name>` — lifecycle
- `tor remove <name> [--force]` — delete
- `tor edit <name> [-p <port>] [-n <nginx-port>] [-t <target-port>] [--auto-ports]` — change ports
- `tor rotate <name>` — new .onion identity
- `tor ssl <service>` — post-hoc HTTPS on a service published over HTTP (canonical self-signed cert `/etc/nginx/ssl/<service>.{crt,key}`, Nginx site to HTTP+HTTPS, `.onion:443` added, same address); error if it already has SSL
- Canonical Tor service names: `<domain>_<name>` — `git_`, `wp_`, `drupal_`, `ghost_`, `magnolia_`, `strapi_`, `wagtail_`, `fileserver_`, `ai_`, and `proxy_` for `tor create web`; the certificate uses the same name and the Nginx site is `proxy_<domain>_<name>` (`fileserver_<name>` for files, `proxy_<name>` for `tor create web`). Unpublishing (`tor remove`, `hide`, `delete`, MCP `tor_remove`) removes the Tor service, its site and its certificate. Services published with v0.9.0 (`git` → `<n>`, `wp` → `proxy_<n>`, CMS → `proxy_<cms>-<n>`) are not recognized: commands say they do not exist. Remove them with `tor remove <old-name>` + publish again (the `.onion` address changes)
- `tor auth list|enable|disable <service>` — client authorization. Every `tor auth` subcommand also accepts `<domain> <instance>` (`tor auth enable ai dev` ≡ `ai_dev`)
- `tor auth add <service> -c <client> -p <pubkey>` / `tor auth revoke <service> -c <client>`
- `tor auth generate -c <client>` — generate x25519 keypair (client side)
- `tor auth rotate <service> -c <client> -p <pubkey>` — replace client public key (client generates the new pair; private key never reaches the operator)

### git — Forgejo Git servers
- Images (new instances): Forgejo 15 LTS; WordPress 6.9 (PHP 8.3) + MariaDB 11.4 LTS; Drupal 11.4 + MariaDB 10.11; Ghost 6 (SQLite); Strapi on Node 22 + PostgreSQL 16 — all pinned by tag + digest, `cap_drop: ALL` + minimal `cap_add`, dedicated Docker networks. Existing instances on EOL images are reported by `doctor --security` (`image-eol`), never migrated automatically.
- `git list` / `git create -n <name> [--ssl] [--http-port] [--ssh-port] [--admin-user <u> --admin-password <p>]`
- `git start|stop|status|delete <name>` — lifecycle
- `git registration <name> --enable|--disable|--status` — user self-registration
- `git edit <name> [--http-port] [--https-port] [--ssh-port] [--auto-ports]`
- `git publish <name> [--ssl] [--auth]` / `git hide <name>` — Tor exposure
- `git user list|create|delete <server> [...]` — user management
- `git watcher` — pipeline watcher (foreground)

### CMS modules — wp, drupal, ghost, magnolia, strapi, wagtail
All share the same lifecycle: `list`, `create --name <n> --http-port <p>`, `start`, `stop`, `status`, `delete [--force]`, `publish [--ssl] [--auth]` (expose on Tor as `<backend>_<name>`), `hide`.
- `wp` — WordPress. Extra: `restart`, `update` (with backup), `config`, `edit [--http-port] [--https-port] [--ssl] [--auto-ports]`. Port range 8080-9000 (auto).
- `drupal` — drupal:10-apache + mariadb:10.11. Extra: `edit --http-port` (atomic container recreation).
- `ghost` — ghost:5-alpine + embedded SQLite, container port 2368. Extra: `edit --http-port`.
- `magnolia` — ghcr.io/magnolia-sre/magnolia-docker/magnolia-docker:latest (Tomcat, Java) with embedded H2 DB. Minimum 1.5 GB RAM (warns if <1536 MB); 4 GB recommended for comfortable operation.
- `strapi` — Node + postgres:16-alpine. 6 per-instance secrets (db_password, app_keys, api_token_salt, admin_jwt_secret, jwt_secret, transfer_token_salt). Extra: `build-image [--force]` (build production image once before first create).
- `wagtail` — wagtail/bakerydemo:latest (demo site) + postgres:16-alpine, container port 8000.

### files — anonymous file sharing
- `files list` / `files create -n <name> [--auth] [--ssl]` / `files edit <name> [-p <port>]` / `files delete <name> --force` / `files fix-perms <name>`
- Files served from `/srv/enola-files/<name>/` via Nginx autoindex over .onion.

### maintenance
- `maintenance status|smoke-test|enable-checks|disable-checks|timer-status|ssh-config`
- `maintenance backup [--keep N]` — system backup; `--keep` overrides retention for this run
- `maintenance backup-config [--max-backups N]` — show or persist retention ([backup].max_backups, env ENOLA_MAX_BACKUPS, default 5)
- `maintenance ssh-harden-pqc [--dry-run] [--force]` — post-quantum SSH KEX (sntrup761x25519-sha512)
- `maintenance cleanup [--target all|logs|docker] [--dry-run] [--force] [--keep-days N]`

### diag — diagnostics
- `diag summary|nginx|tor|ssh|wordpress|wp-sync|nginx-test|resources`
- `diag onion <address.onion> [--format json]` — probes a .onion via Tor SOCKS5h; structured reachability (status, latency, title, failure reason: timeout|proxy_unavailable|site_unreachable)

### ssh — SSH access
- `ssh add-key [--user <name>] -p <pubkey> [--comment <c>]` — append to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys (atomic, deduplicated)
- `ssh deploy-hidden --name <n> --onion-port <p> --local-ssh-port <p>` — publish SSH only via .onion

### test / logs / ports
- `test run [-f filter]|list|benchmark|results|clean`
- `logs list` / `logs view <source> [-l N] [-f]` / `logs install` / `logs smoke-test`
- `ports list [--json]` — every port in the Tor→Nginx→App chain

### firewall — UFW
- `firewall setup [--ssh-port N] [--force]` — deny incoming, allow outgoing, allow SSH, DOCKER-USER chain
- `firewall status` / `firewall allow --port N [--proto tcp|udp|both] [--from CIDR]` / `firewall deny --port N [--proto]`

### apparmor — sandboxing
- `apparmor setup [--mode complain|enforce] [--force]` / `apparmor status`
- `apparmor mode --enforce|--complain|--disable [--profile <name>]`

### vpn — WireGuard
- `vpn create <name> [--port 51820] [--subnet 10.8.0.0/24] [--autostart] [--sync-firewall] [--tor]`
- `vpn list|start|stop|status|delete <name> [--force] [--sync-firewall]`
- `vpn peer add <iface> <peer> --endpoint <host> [--dns <ip>] [--psk] [--ip <ip>] [--tor]`
- `vpn peer add-pubkey <iface> <peer> <pubkey> <ip>` / `vpn peer remove <iface> <pubkey>`

### setup / doctor
- `setup` (core) / `setup --all` (core+VPN+security) / `setup --vpn` / `setup --security` / `setup --pqc-tls` (OpenSSL 3.5 + Nginx PQC stack)
- `doctor` / `doctor --security` (security audit: container hardening, configs, leaked secrets)

### update — advisory feed
- `update check [--json] [--force]` — exit codes: 0 OK, 11 critical advisory, 12 below min_supported, 20 invalid feed, 21 invalid signature
- `update schema [--json]` / `update verify-feed <source> [--signature] [--json]`
- `update download [--yes] [--dry-run] [--json] [--force] [--allow-unsigned]`
- `update apply [--binary <path>] [--json] [--allow-unsigned]`

### verify — post-quantum release verification
- `verify <file> [--pqsig <sig>] [--pubkey <key>] [--json]` — verifies ML-DSA-65 (FIPS 204) signature with the embedded public key; also verifies SHA256 if `<file>.sha256` exists. Offline.

### uninstall
- `uninstall` (dry-run) / `uninstall --yes [--keep-data] [--only binary,config,services,tor,nginx,systemd,apparmor,docker,ufw,data,deps] [--force] [--remove-deps]`

### docs — embedded offline documentation
- `docs quickstart|commands [group]|concepts [topic]|faq [term]|examples [case]|search <term>`
- `docs quantum-security|verify-downloads|security|install-from-iso`

### mcp — MCP server for AI agents
- `mcp` — JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio (NDJSON), protocolVersion `2026-07-28`; methods: initialize, notifications/initialized, ping, tools/list, tools/call, resources/list, resources/read
- flags: `--allow-write` `--allow-tools <CSV>` `--allow-all-mutating` `--max-output-bytes <N>` `--audit-log <path>` `--request-timeout-secs <N>`
- env: `ENOLA_MCP_ALLOW_WRITE` `ENOLA_MCP_ALLOWED_TOOLS` `ENOLA_MCP_MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES` `ENOLA_MCP_AUDIT_LOG` `ENOLA_MCP_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECS`; TOML `[mcp]` in ~/.enola/config.toml; precedence flag > env > file > defaults (allow_write=false, max_output_bytes=65536, audit_log=stderr, request_timeout_secs=60)
- policy: read-only by default; mutating tools need `--allow-write` (+ mandatory `--allow-tools` allowlist; an empty allowlist requires the explicit `--allow-all-mutating`, which prints a warning); destructive tools additionally require a single-use `confirm_token` bound to tool+args (two-step, 300s TTL); `try_run: true` simulates mutating/destructive tools without side effects; `mcp` family is never dispatchable via enola_run_command
- 21 tools: 13 read-only (config_show, diag_nginx, diag_summary, diag_tor, doctor, plan_tor_create, plan_wp_create, ports_list, tor_list, update_check, verify_onion, wp_list, wp_status), 4 mutating (files_create, tor_create, wp_create, wp_publish), 2 destructive (tor_remove, wp_hide; require `"force": true` + confirm_token), 2 meta (enola_list_commands, enola_run_command); all schemas reject unknown args (additionalProperties: false) and out-of-range values
- resources: 36 embedded user docs, URIs `enola://docs/<path>`
- stdout carries ONLY JSON-RPC; logs/diagnostics go to stderr

### ask — local AI assistant (Ollama)
- `ask <prompt> [--model <m>] [--endpoint <url>] [--instance <name>] [--no-exec] [--yes]` — natural-language assistant backed by local Ollama (`/api/chat` with tools, `/api/tags`, `/api/pull`), sharing the MCP `ToolRegistry`
- config: `[ai]` in `~/.enola/config.toml` (`endpoint`, `model`, `timeout_secs`, `use_tor_for_downloads`) and env vars `ENOLA_AI_ENDPOINT`, `ENOLA_AI_MODEL`, `ENOLA_AI_TIMEOUT_SECS`, `ENOLA_AI_USE_TOR_DOWNLOADS`; precedence flag > env > file > defaults (`http://127.0.0.1:11434`, `llama3.1:8b`, `120`, `false`)
- gate: `ReadOnly` tools run directly; `Mutating`/`Destructive` tools require an interactive TTY `[s/N]` confirmation showing sanitized arguments (`--yes` approves `Mutating` only — `Destructive` always needs the TTY prompt, even with `--yes`; fails closed without TTY), or `--no-exec` to simulate via `try_run` without side effects
- MCP meta-keys (`confirm_token`, `try_run`) are stripped from schemas sent to the local LLM; `ask` is in `FORBIDDEN_FAMILIES` so `enola_run_command` never dispatches `ask` recursively

### ai — local AI instances (Ollama + Open WebUI)
- `ai create --name <n> [--model <m>] [--api-port <p>] [--webui-port <p>] [--no-gpu] [--memory-gb <gb>] [--no-pull]` — deploys `enola-ai-<n>-ollama` and `enola-ai-<n>-webui` bound to `127.0.0.1` over `ContainerPort` (Bollard) with `flock` port locks, calibrated limits (`memory_limit >= 8 GiB`, `pids_limit >= 4096`), and NVIDIA GPU detection via `EnolaHardwareProbe`
- `ai list` / `ai status <n>` / `ai start <n>` / `ai stop <n>` / `ai delete <n> --force` / `ai logs <n> [--lines N]` (also via `logs view ai-<n>`)
- `ai publish <n> [--ssl] [--auth] [--verify]` / `ai hide <n>` — exposes/removes Open WebUI as the `.onion` service `ai_<n>` via Nginx + Tor (and verifies SOCKS5h reachability with `--verify`); the JSON result adds `https_port` (with `--ssl`) and `auth_enabled`
- `ai model list|download|import|add|delete|validate|refresh` — per-instance GGUF library at `/srv/enola-ai/<n>/ollama/models-gguf/`; download (HF `org/repo --file` or URL) streams to `<file>.part` (Range resume only from `.part`) + SHA-256 and GGUF header check before an atomic rename (a previous model with the same name is never touched on failure), registers via `/api/create` unless `--no-register`; `add` pulls `/api/pull` for registry refs or registers library `.gguf`; `delete` needs `--force` (Destructive); downloads default to clearnet, `--tor`/`use_tor_for_downloads` forces SOCKS5h and reports the route
- `ai rag status|ingest|ingest-docs|bind|sync|config` — per-instance vector store (`enola-ai-<n>-chromadb`|`-qdrant`) lazily provisioned via `ContainerPort` on `127.0.0.1` (ports 12001–12500, flock, `/srv/enola-ai/<n>/<backend>/`, 1 GiB/512 pids); ingest chunks with presets `docs|code|faq|large` and Ollama `/api/embed` (`nomic-embed-text`; if Ollama is down ingestion fails closed — TTY offers retry/hash/cancel — and hash embeddings only via explicit `--embedding-fallback hash`; each collection records its method in `rag_config.json` `embedding_kinds` and mixing is refused; queries use the recorded method); `bind` (Destructive, `--force`, canonicalize + system-dir denylist) registers `git|filesystem|wordpress` sources; `sync` re-ingests (git pull as invoking user, WP REST posts); `ingest-docs` (Mutating) rebuilds collection `enola_docs` from the embedded docs (same embedding policy); `docs_lookup` MCP tool (ReadOnly) queries only `enola_docs` semantically, never the user index, and degrades to empty results plus a note when the docs are not indexed
- `ai benchmark <n> [--model m] [--prompt p] [--runs n]` — local generation benchmark: tokens/s from Ollama `eval_count`/`eval_duration` (wall-clock fallback), avg latency, model size (Mutating)
- `ai provider list|status|set|remove|test` + `ask --provider <p>` — external BYOK cloud (`openai|anthropic|grok|groq|openrouter`), the only path where data leaves the machine; disabled by default; consent gate (TTY `[s/N]` or `--accept-risks`, fails closed); keys in `~/.enola/providers.env` (atomic 0600, never logged/argv — TTY prompt or `--key-stdin`); `--tor`/`ENOLA_AI_TOR_PROXY`/`[ai].tor_proxy` forces SOCKS5h; `ask --provider` single-shot without tools; `provider list|status` ReadOnly, `remove` Destructive
- `ai finetune prepare|validate|start|status|register|wizard` — JSONL datasets (`alpaca|chatml|sharegpt|text`) → canonical ChatML + deterministic split (`prepare`); pre-flight schema/VRAM/`HardwareProbePort` checks (`validate`); `start` resolves the base model against the instance GGUF library (default `inst.model` by index `name`; `--base-model` accepts `name` or `.gguf` filename; clear error if absent), pre-validates the GGUF header (`general.architecture`/`general.file_type`, supported-quant hint on failure) and mounts GGUF + HF tokenizer as volumes (`/model.gguf`, `/tokenizer`), with `--tokenizer <org/repo>` overriding the tokenizer repo (host-side on-demand download); isolated training container `enola-ai-<n>-finetune-<job>` via `ContainerPort` (no ports/net, `enola-finetune:latest`, 16 GiB/4096 pids, ro-rootfs, GPU, `--low-memory`) running embedded `train_lora.py` (`include_str!` → `/srv/enola-ai/<n>/finetune/<job>/scripts/`, model via `gguf_file` + tokenizer via `AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(dir)`); `start` Destructive (`--force`), `status` ReadOnly, `register <n> <job_id>` (Mutating) imports the exported `.gguf` of a `Completed` job into the GGUF library (SHA-256 + header) and registers it in Ollama (`/api/create`) as `<name>-ft`, `wizard` FORBIDDEN_PATHS

### Other
- `license [--third-party]` — full license text; `--third-party` prints the copyright notices and license texts of the third-party software embedded in the binary
- `quickref` — Docker ↔ Enola equivalence table
- `web [--port 8090]` — local web dashboard, binds to 127.0.0.1, token-protected. Its console (`/api/console/run`) applies the same command policy as the MCP server (refuses `web`, `mcp`, `setup`, `uninstall`, `ssh`, `ask`, `update apply`, `test run`; destructive commands need `"confirm"`); the web API cannot install a custom or unsigned binary (CLI-only)
- `config-show [--json]` / `config-validate [--reachable] [--json]` — centralized config (`~/.enola/config.toml`), priority: CLI flag > env var > file > default
- `plan wp create -n <name> [--http-port <p>]` / `plan git create -n <name> [--ssl] [--http-port] [--ssh-port]` / `plan tor create -n <name> [-s web|static|files|raw] [-p <virtual-port>] [-t <target-port>] [--ssl]` — dry-run: shows the change plan (ports, containers, paths, UFW rules, AppArmor profile, risk level) WITHOUT executing anything. 0 side effects. Output: text or `--format json`.

## Key concepts

- Hidden service types: `web` (Tor→Nginx→App, recommended), `static` (Tor→Nginx, files from /var/www/<name>), `files` (Nginx autoindex), `raw` (Tor→App direct TCP, for SSH/databases).
- Everything is localhost-only: internal ports are never exposed to the network; visitors only ever see the .onion address.
- Tor client authorization uses x25519 keypairs (like SSH keys): client generates, sends public key to operator, operator authorizes.
- Post-quantum measures: ML-DSA-65 release signatures, optional ML-KEM hybrid TLS stack (`setup --pqc-tls`), WireGuard preshared keys (`--psk`), SSH sntrup761x25519 KEX (`ssh-harden-pqc`), Tor auth key rotation.
- Update security: advisory feed signed with minisign; binaries verified with SHA256 + minisign before applying; stable exit codes for scripting. At euid 0 (`sudo`), `[update]` is read only from root-owned `/etc/enola/config.toml` (`~/.enola/config.toml` is ignored).
- Input validation: VPN peer names (1–32 `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`) and peer IPs (plain IPv4 inside the server subnet) are validated in the application layer for CLI/web/MCP; the update feed is refused if its signed `published_at` is older than the newest one already accepted (warning when > 90 days old); manifest entries reject line breaks/NUL (and `|` in keys) and `uninstall.sh` only removes paths under Enola-managed locations.
- Web dashboard hardening: `Host` must be a loopback name (else 421, anti DNS-rebinding; port not checked so SSH tunnels work); strict CSP `default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'` (no `'unsafe-inline'`; no inline handlers or styles in the UI), `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `nosniff`, `no-referrer`, `no-store` on `/api`; the token rotates every 12 h (`[web].token_ttl_secs`) and is rewritten to `~/.enola/web-token`, plus `POST /api/token/rotate`. `ask` with a non-local LLM endpoint asks `[s/N]` before every read-only tool that can reveal host data (default-deny; docs/catalog/plan exempt).
- Running as root (`sudo`): inherited environment is an allowlist — only `ENOLA_ACCEPT_LICENSE`, `ENOLA_MCP_CHILD` and `ENOLA_AUTO_SETUP` survive; every other `ENOLA_*` is dropped with one aggregated warning (names only) and `PATH` is reset to a fixed safe value. Flags are always honoured (`--tor-socks` to a non-loopback proxy prints a warning). Security keys (`[ai].endpoint`, `[ai].tor_proxy`, `[distribution].*`, `[update].*`, `[mcp].*`, non-loopback `[http].tor_socks_proxy`) are read only from root-owned `/etc/enola/config.toml`; convenience keys still come from `~/.enola/config.toml`. `update download/apply --allow-unsigned` is the only way to skip signature verification (`ENOLA_ALLOW_UNSIGNED_UPDATE` was removed); the dashboard token is always random (`ENOLA_WEB_TOKEN` was removed); as root the MCP audit log must live in `/var/log/enola/` or `/var/lib/enola/`; `ask` prints the effective LLM endpoint and its source. Test-only variables (`ENOLA_SKIP_ROOT_CHECK`, `ENOLA_APPARMOR_ENABLED_PATH`, `ENOLA_MANIFEST_PATH`, `ENOLA_TEST_*`) exist only in `--features testing` builds. Full table: docs/user/general/config-reference.md, "Variables solo-desarrollo".
- MCP server security: read-only by default; mutating tools require explicit `--allow-write` plus a mandatory allowlist (or explicit `--allow-all-mutating`) (`--allow-tools`/`ENOLA_MCP_ALLOWED_TOOLS`/`[mcp].allowed_tools`, tool names or `family:sub` paths); destructive tools demand `"force": true` AND a two-step `confirm_token` (single-use, bound to exact args, 300s TTL, not surviving restarts); mutating/destructive calls are audit-logged (requested/rejected/simulated/confirmation_requested/authorized/ok/error) with secret redaction. `enola_run_command` never dispatches the `mcp`, `ask`, `ssh`, `uninstall`, `web`, `setup` families nor `update apply`, `test run`, `test benchmark`, nor the secret-printing `tor auth generate`, `vpn peer add`, `git user create` (same gate for the web console `/api/console/run`); dispatched subprocesses get a cleared env plus allowlist; at euid 0 the `[mcp]` section is read only from root-owned `/etc/enola/config.toml`.
